items.title: Manny Albam interviewed by Monk Rowe, Tarrytown, New York, October 31, 1998
items.q: And we used to sometimes hook up at various projects and all that, and we had the same answering service and a little room that you could go to to change your clothes or something.

ctx.x: We didn’t talk about the jingle scene. © Fillius Jazz Archive -21-

I’ll give you a clue as to the — I did Coca Cola, I did Chevrolet, I did a whole bunch of things. And this is a clue as to how people think in the advertising business, or try to think. We were doing a project for I think it was cosmetics. It was a female product of one kind or another. And they called me in and we started talking about a month before the recording session about what would be nice. I said, “well I’d love to use a string quartet and a harp and maybe an unamplified guitar, a classical guitar and a…
You seem to have certainly survived the rock & roll onslaught. Did it change your work at all when rock & roll became the popular music? © Fillius Jazz Archive -22-
